rows.description: A toddler in a joint household is passed between grandparents, aunts and cousins and feels safe with many familiar faces. Crying is soothed by whoever is nearest, so attachment spreads across several people.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler in a nuclear home is tied closely to one or two caregivers and shows sharper distress when they leave the room. Fewer faces means deeper but narrower bonds and quieter days.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child among cousins learns to share toys, beds and food without being asked, and also learns to fight and make up quickly. Belonging is taken for granted; privacy is a word not yet needed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child hears that a cousin scored higher or behaves better and feels a mix of motivation and hurt. Constant family comparison can build drive or a quiet sense of never being enough.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A grandmother notices grandchildren copying her prayers, stories and sayings and feels her role has meaning. Daily contact passes on language and values that a nuclear family may have to seek out deliberately.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager in a crowded joint home wants a closed door and a phone call without ears nearby. Asking for space feels selfish next to family closeness, so it comes out as sulking or slamming doors.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager in a small nuclear family with working parents feels the quiet, with no grandparent or cousin to talk to after school. Freedom is real but so is the loneliness, and screens fill the gap.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult finds that a course or job choice is discussed by uncles and aunts before they have decided. It feels like care and control together; a wise reply thanks them, listens, and still owns the final choice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An elder sees children wanting smaller households and feels the joint family slipping away. A wise elder accepts new shapes of family while asking for regular gatherings and kindness rather than duty by force.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young working adult wants a separate flat and fears being seen as abandoning parents. Guilt and independence pull together; honest talk about visits and duties eases the shift more than a sudden announcement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
